title: Best Golf Umbrellas UK
short: Six golf umbrellas tested in the rain and wind on course, compared on canopy size, wind resistance and grip.
intro: A golf umbrella needs to be big enough to cover you and your bag, sturdy enough not to turn inside out in the wind, and comfortable to hold with wet or gloved hands. This guide is based on Golf Monthly's tested roundup (updated July 2026), where the team played golf in the rain and wind to judge overall protection, strength, and how easy each umbrella was to open, close and store. No manufacturer receives preferential treatment.

products.name: 64" Double Canopy Umbrella
products.best_for: Golfers who want a tour-proven umbrella with instant auto-open protection
products.key_spec: 64in double canopy, auto-open, fibreglass shaft, WindPro technology
products.summary: Golf Monthly notes this is commonly seen on tour among TaylorMade-sponsored players. The auto-open feature gives immediate relief when rain hits, and WindPro technology is designed to counter strong winds and prevent the umbrella turning inside out. The lightweight fibreglass shaft adds durability. It's only available in one colour.

products.name: 68" Auto Umbrella
products.best_for: Golfers who want maximum coverage and a colour to match their bag
products.key_spec: 68in double canopy, auto-open, slip-resistant rubber grip, fits Sun Mountain bag handles
products.summary: Golf Monthly found elite protection for the wettest and warmest conditions from the double canopy, with a rubber, slip-resistant grip that helps with damp hands or waterproof gloves. Available in six colours and large enough that a playing partner can shelter underneath alongside you. The handle is designed to fit Sun Mountain bags specifically.
cons: Different colours offer varied protection ratings

products.name: DryJoys Double Canopy Golf Umbrella
products.best_for: Golfers who want a large, fully waterproof umbrella from a trusted waterproofing brand
products.key_spec: 68in double canopy, 100% waterproof, soft handle, includes storage sheath
products.summary: Golf Monthly notes FootJoy's expertise in waterproof gear shows here: a huge 68in canopy offers lightweight, fully waterproof protection with a soft handle for grip and comfort in tricky conditions. The double canopy counters high winds by overlapping the bottom layer, helping prevent the umbrella turning inside out, and it comes with a storage sheath. It's only available in one colour.
pros: Fully waterproof, comes with a storage sheath
products.search: FootJoy DryJoys Double Canopy Golf Umbrella

products.name: Jet Black Tour Double Canopy Golf Umbrella
products.best_for: Golfers who regularly battle windy courses and want anti-inversion protection
products.key_spec: 68in double canopy, anti-inversion system, UV protection
products.summary: Golf Monthly's pick for golfers who regularly battle the wind: the 68in double canopy is designed to prevent the umbrella blowing inside out in high winds, and UV protection also provides shade on hot, humid days. It's the style seen carried by many caddies on the PGA Tour. The handle is smaller than some rivals.
products.search: Titleist Jet Black Tour Double Canopy Golf Umbrella

products.name: Shield Double Canopy Umbrella
products.best_for: Golfers who play in blustery conditions and want a non-slip grip for rain gloves
products.key_spec: 64in double canopy, fibreglass shaft, non-slip handle
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the Shield holds its own in blustery conditions, strong and robust thanks to a fibreglass shaft and ergonomic frame built to battle tough elements. The non-slip handle is a nice touch for golfers who wear rain gloves and don't want to remove them between shots. It may be a bit too big for some.
cons: May be a bit too big for some

products.name: 68" Tour Umbrella
products.best_for: Emergency, quick-deploy protection when a sudden storm hits
products.summary: Golf Monthly calls this great emergency protection for when a surprise heavy storm hits: the foam handle is comfortable to hold and a simple release deployment gives quick cover the moment rain starts hammering down. It's the version seen on the PGA Tour among Ping-sponsored players. It only comes in white, and sits at a premium price point.

guide.a: A double canopy, like all the umbrellas here, has two layers of material with air vents that let a little wind through, designed specifically to stop the umbrella turning inside out on blustery links courses. A single canopy is lighter but offers less wind resistance.

guide.q: What size canopy do I need?
guide.a: Most golf umbrellas run 64 to 68 inches. A larger canopy, like the 68in models from Sun Mountain, FootJoy, Titleist and Ping, gives more coverage, useful if you use a trolley and want to shelter your bag too, but adds weight. Decide where your happy medium lies before buying.

Yes, especially in the rain or with wet gloves. The Sun Mountain and Callaway both have rubber, non-slip grips designed for wet or gloved hands, while the Ping uses a comfortable foam handle for quick emergency deployment.

If you play somewhere sunny as often as somewhere wet, a UV-protected umbrella like the Titleist Jet Black Tour keeps you cool in the shade and helps protect skin from harmful rays, not just from rain.
